alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism likely driving weight gain
alerts.message: Patient has TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target <4.5) with low Free T4, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, delayed ankle reflexes, constipation, and cold intolerance — classic hypothyroidism. She reports often forgetting her levothyroxine. The clinician attributes 9 kg weight gain to DTG and plans to switch, but poorly controlled hypothyroidism is a more likely cause. DTG-associated weight gain is well recognised, but this patient's profound hypothyroid symptoms predate any DTG switch consideration and strongly suggest inadequate thyroid replacement. Switching off DTG without first correcting hypothyroidism risks unnecessary ART change with no resolution of the underlying problem.

evidence.recommended_action: Address levothyroxine adherence and up-titrate dose to normalise TSH before attributing weight gain to DTG. Reassess weight and symptoms after thyroid optimisation before considering ART switch.

alerts.title: DTG hyperglycaemia risk factors require glucose monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines require screening for hyperglycaemia risk factors before DTG use: age ≥40, BMI ≥25, hypertension history, or family history of DM. This patient has multiple risk factors — age 45, BMI 33 — warranting glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first 12 months. Fasting glucose today is 5.6 mmol/L (below the >6.95 threshold for contraindication). However, no 3-monthly glucose monitoring is documented since DTG initiation in January 2023, representing a monitoring gap. The elevated lipids (LDL 4.2, total cholesterol 6.4, triglycerides 2.3) further compound metabolic risk alongside obesity and hypothyroidism.

evidence.recommended_action: Continue DTG but implement 3-monthly glucose monitoring for the first 12 months. Address metabolic risk through weight management, thyroid optimisation, and lipid monitoring.

alerts.title: TDF renal monitoring overdue by >12 months
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR every 12 months for experienced patients on TDF. The last creatinine was 72 umol/L on 2025-08-12, 196 days before today's visit — over 6 months ago. No renal function test has been ordered today, and the clinician's plan does not include creatinine or eGFR monitoring. This is a guideline-mandated annual monitoring gap.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR now to fulfil the annual TDF renal monitoring requirement.

gher genetic barrier of DTG means patients are less likely to develop resistance and therefore postponing the need for superior line treatment ## 6.6 SCREENING FOR RISK FACTORS PRIOR TO INITIATING DGT DTG is a very well-tolerated drug, with lower overall adverse effects when compared to other drugs like EFV. Hyperglycemia among previously non-diabetic adults and worsening of hyperglycemia among diabetics has been reported among clients on DTG. Although the hyperglycemia associated with DTG has been reported among clients newly initiated on ART as well as among those already on ART and transitioned to DTG-based regimens, the hyperglycemia appears to occur more commonly among the latter group. Adults being initiated on DTG should be screened for risk factors for hyperglycemia: * Age ≥ 40 years * BMI≥ 24 kg/m2 * History of hypertension * Known diabetics should not be initiated or transitioned to DTG. Give an EFV400 or an ATV/r-based regimen. * Clients with 2 or more risk factors for hyperglycemia and a high baseline RBS or FBS should not be initiated/transitioned to DTG. Give an EFV400 or ATZ/r-based regimen.
